Clarity.output:
Dear Ms. O,

Chocolate can cause acne when you eat a lot of it. The more chocolate you eat, the more you'll likely see pimples. Acne is usually associated with overconsumption of chocolate or foods with a high glycemic index (GI). The GI measures how quickly food is converted into sugar. The higher the GI, the faster your blood sugar rises. A high GI diet can cause acne in people who have predisposing factors such as hormonal imbalances (polycystic ovarian syndrome, etc.) or are taking certain medications.

Many of my patients ask me if they should completely avoid chocolate to prevent skin problems. The answer is no. Chocolate is an important source of antioxidants and can be beneficial to your health. However, you should consider your body's response to chocolate before eating it. If you experience skin problems after eating chocolate, it's probably best to avoid it.

Sincerely,

Dr. Jennifer Chwalek

Clarity.input: I've heard that drinking eight glasses of water a day is essential for good health. Should I strictly adhere to this rule?
Clarity.output:
Yes, you should adhere to this rule so long as you are healthy and do not have a medical condition or take any drugs that require you to restrict your water intake.

The human body is about 60% water, and water is the most important and basic nutrient. Water is lost in the urine, breath, sweat, and feces. Water is necessary for every bodily function, including digestion and elimination. Water also helps regulate our body temperature and keeps our skin from drying out. Water is needed to transport nutrients to the cells, and is part of the fluid that transports waste away from the cells.

Your body constantly needs a supply of water, and this is why you should drink at least eight glasses of water a day. You should always be thirsty. If you are not thirsty, you are probably dehydrated. To keep hydrated, you should drink water throughout the day. If you don't like water, then drink flavored water, or add a slice of lemon or lime.

You should also drink water before, during, and after exercise. Your body temperature rises during exercise, so water is needed to keep from overheating. Water is also lost in sweat.

If you eat a lot of fruits and vegetables, and have a balanced diet, you don't have to drink eight glasses of water a day. However, if you eat a high-protein diet, or eat foods that contain a lot of salt or sugar, you should drink more water to flush these toxins from your body.

Also, if you live in a hot, dry climate or in a dry area where the air is very dry, you should drink more water.

If you have a medical condition or take any drugs, you should consult your doctor before strictly adhering to the eight-glasses-a-day rule. Some medical conditions require you to restrict your water intake.

Some drugs also cause your body to retain water, and you may need to restrict your water intake when taking these drugs.
